about: Features added to Heresay since apps were first installed. An agent in a connected repo checks these with whats_new, tells the person what's new, and asks before adding any. `detect` is what the code contains once a feature is in; `platforms` limits it to those apps; `sign_in` limits it to apps that answered that. `when` (optional, strings, or an object keyed by web/swift): offer the feature only if the code contains any of them. `detect` may be keyed the same way. `offer`: recommended (offer on its own) or optional (offered only right after a version update that introduced it).

changes.title: Open the Report panel next to the app's own Report button (optional)
changes.summary: When the app opens Heresay from its own Report, Feedback or Help item, the panel opens as a centred window with the page dimmed. That is the recommended default, so most apps need nothing. If the person prefers it right beside that item, set data-panel="beside" (web) or add .heresayAnchor() to the button (Swift). Ask: centred window (recommended) or next to your button?

how.web: guide customize-web, How it opens (data-panel="beside" on the script tag)

changes.title: Put the Heresay mark in the app's own Report button (optional)
changes.summary: The app has its own Report, Feedback or Help button. Adding the Heresay mark to it (mark plus label, or a round mark-only button) makes it recognisable from app to app. Web: an empty inside the button. Swift: HeresayMarkIcon() in a Label. Ask: add the mark to your button?

how.web: guide customize-web, The mark in your own button
how.ios: guide customize-apple, The mark in your own button
how.macos: guide customize-apple, The mark in your own button

changes.title: Pick another Report panel layout
changes.summary: Three layouts exist: composer (type pills and a text box; the default and recommended for most apps), steps (guided rows; consumer apps) and bar (a compact floating bar; dense pro tools). Only worth changing if the app clearly fits another.

changes.title: Get crash reports without anyone sending them
changes.summary: With crashReports: .send, a Mac or iOS app reports a run that ended badly (a crash, a hang, running out of memory, a force quit) by itself at the next launch, with what happened before it and how it crashed. It arrives even when the app crashes on every launch, as long as Heresay.configure runs first. It waits in the inbox for a person like any report. Off until the app turns it on; it sends diagnostics without asking, so the app's privacy details should say so.

changes.title: Offer help when someone seems stuck
changes.summary: A small note by the Report button asks “Something not working?” when someone presses a button again and again with nothing happening, hits an error right after a click, or sees requests fail (web), clicks a disabled control again and again (macOS), or comes back after a crash (iOS and macOS). And “Stuck on something?” when someone seems unsure: typing that stopped, going back and forth between the same few pages or screens, a field refused again and again. It opens the form as Broken or Confusing, with what happened attached. Watched on the device, never sent; once per visit, and quiet for a week after “Not now”. Off until the app turns it on.

changes.title: Make Heresay fit the app
changes.summary: The Swift package takes a HeresayStyle: another corner or clear a tab bar, say “Feedback” instead of “Report”, a quieter button, the app's light or dark theme, French, Tamil or Hindi, a half-height or full-screen sheet, or only some report types. The dashboard's Design page shows each choice and gives the Swift.

changes.title: Make the Report button fit the app
changes.summary: The web widget can take the app's colour (the logo follows it), sit in another corner or clear a chat bubble, say “Feedback” instead of “Report”, follow the app's light or dark theme, speak French, Tamil or Hindi, or have no floating button when the app has its own feedback menu item. The dashboard's Design page shows each choice on the real widget.

changes.title: Tell people Heresay is there
changes.summary: A one-time introduction, so the people using the app know they can report things. On macOS it names Help › Report a Problem… (⌥⌘R), on iOS the Report button, on the web a bubble over the button. Shown once per device.

changes.title: Signed-in people are never asked who they are
changes.summary: When the app tells Heresay who is signed in (id, name, email), the report form stops asking for a name and email, and the team can reply to them.
